subject: Demo follow-up: Brightwell integration playbook (streaming funcalls, embeddings + rerank)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@brightwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Demo follow-up: Brightwell integration playbook (streaming funcalls, embeddings + rerank)

Hi Asha — thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we loop engineering in.

Key pain points you reiterated:
- Inconsistent relevancy on search results for clinical notes (current embed + sparse baseline) — recall drop at long tail queries.
- Tight latency SLO: 150ms p95 for single-message triage flows.
- Need for streaming responses in the triage UI and server-side reranking to surface confidence signals.

Primary goals we agreed on:
1) Pilot: embeddings + rerank on ~2M clinical snippets to measure recall uplift and token-cost delta.
2) Maintain p95 < 200ms for interactive flows during pilot using batching + prefix KV cache.
3) Evaluate streaming function-calls for structured triage outputs (JSON fields) to reduce client-side parsing work.

Proposed approach (high level):
- SDK changes: add a light wrapper to emit streaming funcall events and an optional structured-output schema. I've attached a small patch that shows the proposed surface (sdk-proposed-diff.patch).
- Model & infra: start with a mid-sized embedding model + a lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) hosted in a Dedicated pool for predictable p95. Redwood will provide a quantization recommendation and batching profile for your dataset.
- Operational: mutual action plan (MAP) with 4-week pilot, weekly checkpoints, and two eval prompt sets. Link to MAP in related links.

Immediate asks from Brightwell:
- Confirm sample dataset access (S3 link or sharepoint) and retention constraints.
- Sign off on pilot scope (embeddings size, reranker candidate, and latency SLO).
- Availability for a technical kickoff with your platform engineer (30–45m) next week.

Attachments included: BRIGHTWELL-POC-plan.pdf (pilot milestones), sdk-proposed-diff.patch (minimal API change), streaming-funcall-diagram.png (call flow).

If that all looks right, can you confirm the dataset access method and whether Friday 10am PT for a kickoff works?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

From: Asha Menon <asha@brightwell.com>

Date: 2027-04-28T17:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: Brightwell integration playbook (streaming funcalls, embeddings + rerank)

Thanks Jordan — very helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications: 

1) Dataset: we can share a 2M snippet S3 bucket (read-only) with a short retention policy (90 days). Is that sufficient for the pilot?
2) Latency SLO: your note said p95 < 200ms as a goal — our product team would prefer we aim for <=150ms p95 if possible for the triage UI. Is that realistic within the pilot if we use dedicated capacity?
3) Function-calls: our platform engineer (cc'd from integrations) wants to understand the schema you propose for structured outputs. Can you include a small example JSON schema?

Friday 10am PT works for a kickoff call. We can confirm the invite once we have the smaller schema example.

— Asha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-28T18:02:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Demo follow-up: Brightwell integration playbook (streaming funcalls, embeddings + rerank)

Jordan — forwarding Asha's questions. Quick internal notes: 

- Dataset retention: 90 days is fine for the pilot as long as Brightwell confirms no PHI beyond redacted clinical snippets — ops needs to sign the data access form.
- Latency: with Dedicated and KV caching we can realistically target 140–160ms p95 on their triage traffic shape; 150ms should be achievable but depends on rewrite overhead and reranker hop. We'll need to reserve a 1-pad of capacity for the first week to tune batching.

Action items I can take:
- Prepare a minimal JSON schema example for funcall streaming (2–3 fields + confidence).
- Draft the infra plan for Dedicated pool sizing and initial quantization suggestion.

Kimberly — can you confirm engineering availability Friday 10am PT? If not, propose alternates.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha@brightwell.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-29T08:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: Brightwell integration playbook (streaming funcalls, embeddings + rerank)

Hi Asha — thanks for the quick replies and the Friday confirmation. Answers inline and a small example schema below.

1) Dataset: S3 read-only with 90-day retention works. We'll send a short Data Access Agreement and S3 role instructions after you confirm the S3 URI.

2) Latency: as Ben noted, with a Dedicated pool and prefix KV caching we expect to get into the 140–160ms p95 range for your baseline triage shape. To hit 150ms p95 consistently we'll:
   - Reserve a small dedicated slot for the pilot week so we can tune batch sizing.
   - Use an embedding+light reranker flow (reranker only invoked for top-K candidates).
   - Apply quantization settings we validated on similar workloads.

3) Function-call schema (example):
{
  \"intent\": \"triage_issue\",  // enum: triage_issue | escalate | info_lookup
  \"severity\": \"low|medium|high\",
  \"identified_entities\": [\"med_term1\", \"med_term2\"],
  \"confidence\": 0.92
}

This will be emitted as streaming funcall events so the UI can start rendering fields before completion; we will also include an event indicating finality. The sdk-proposed-diff.patch shows the client API change: an onFuncCall callback + a fallback non-streaming call.

Next steps / immediate asks (action checklist):
- Asha: share S3 URI and confirm data classification (PII/PHI).
- Brightwell integrations: nominate the platform engineer for the kickoff (Friday 10am PT).
- Ben / Kimberly: prepare the Dedicated sizing doc and short quantization note (Ben will take the sizing; Kimberly to validate the expected p95 on their test harness).

I'll drop the MAP link into the invite and include the BRIGHTWELL-POC-plan.pdf in the calendar.

If that aligns, I'll send the calendar invite for Friday 10am PT and include a short pre-read.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
